title.narrative: South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation Power Transmission and Distribution System Strengthening Project

description.narrative: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) will provide a loan to the Government of Nepal (the government) to (a) upgrade 220/132 kilovolt (kV) substations to 400/220/132 kV substations to enable electricity generated from independent power producer (IPPs) plants in the Khimti hydropower corridor to be exported to India; (b) construction of three 132/11 kV substations in Teku, Koteshwor, and Thapathali which will increase supply capacity into the Kathmandu Valley; (c) modernizing and reinforcing four distribution centers around Kathmandu Valley to be able to meet increasing domestic demand for electricity; and (d) construction of 33 kV, 11 kV, and 0.4 kV lines and substations to facilitate connection of approximately 150,000 new customers in Nepal's Province 2 in the country's southeast region The proposed project complements the efforts of Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) to strengthen parts of Nepal's high-voltage transmission network and complete Nepal's portion of the second cross-border transmission line with India for increasing electricity trade.

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Distribution system in the Kathmandu Valley, Bharatpur, and Pokhara, and consumers awareness on energy efficiency and safety improved. Indicator: 10 new 33/11 kV substations, 350 circuit-km of 33 kV lines, 1,000 circuit-km of 11 kV lines, and 960 circuit-km of low-voltage lines commissioned in Province 2 (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: The contract was divided into 5 lots and all were awarded to M/s Tata Projects Limited, India.
Lot 1: Construction of six (6) nos. of new 33/11kV substations and 97 ckt km of 33kV line- Saptari, Siraha & Dhanusa Districts: Work is progressing well.
Lot-2: Construction of four (4) nos. of new 33/11kV substations and 226 ckt km of 33kV line- Mahottari, Sarlahi, Rautahat, Bara & Parsa Districts: As of 30 June 2025, the physical progress is 80%.
Lot-3 : Construction of 250 ckt km of 11kV line, 320 ckt km of 400V line and Installation of 150 nos. of Distribution Transformers - Saptari & Siraha Districts: Work is progressing well
Lot-4 : Construction of 360 ckt km of 11kV line, 350 ckt km of 400V line and Installation of 175 nos. of Distribution Transformers - Dhanusa, Mahottari & Sarlahi Districts: Work is progressing but not as expected.
Lot-5 : Construction of 340 ckt km of 11kV line, 330 ckt km of 400V line and Installation of 175 nos. of Distribution Transformers - Rautahat, Bara & Parsa Districts: Work progress is very slow than expected. Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:

NEA to secure land at Balkumari by 31 October 2025.

Output: Indicator Indicator: 12 km 132 kV double-circuit transmission line from Bhaktapur to Koteshwor, and 2 km 66 kV transmission line from Koteshwor to Banewsor commissioned (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Package A1.1-Construction of 132 kV underground transmission line and 132/66/11kV substation at Koteshwor: This package includes construction of 132/11kV substation at Thimi and Koteshwor. Due to unavailability of land at Koteshwor, NEA has planned to construct the S/S at DWSS's land at Balkumari/Koteshwor. NEA to secure land at Balkumari and submit bidding document and safeguard reports to ADB by 31 October 2025.
Package A1.2- Construction of 132 kV line from Bhaktapur substation to Thimi substation and bay addition works at Bhaktapur substation: The package includes 132 kV double circuit underground line from Thimi Substation to Balkumari Substation, and 66 kV LILO of existing Baneshwor-Bhaktapur-Patan line. The contract for this package was awarded to KEC International Limited of India on 14 December 2022.
Overall 70% physical progress achieved as of end September 2025. Work progress is slow, and construction work affected due to delay in road cutting permits. In October 2025, the road cutting permit has been resolved, and work is expected to progress well Data Source: NEA reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 9 distribution centers in the Kathmandu Valley, the Bharatpur distribution center in Chitwan district, and the Pokhara distribution center in Kaski district reinforced and modernized (2019 baseline: 0) (TI 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Two packages awarded: (i) distribution system reinforcement and modernization of Easter-western part of Kathmandu Valley - package awarded to the M/S Larsen & Toubro Limited, India, on 24 June 2020 with a contract closing date of 19 December 2023.
